source_title: Producers Shift to Make More Lower-Carbon Portland-Limestone Cement
evidence_summary: Retrospective reporting dates initial US commercial PLC production to 2005 and attributes early demand to private development.
interpretation_limit: Retrospective industry account; no plant attribution or manufacturer cost estimate.

source_title: Holcim VP Recognized by Portland Cement Association
evidence_summary: PCA credited a Holcim executive with work toward AASHTO/ASTM limestone cement acceptance and claimed resulting industry-wide savings of millions of dollars per year.
interpretation_limit: Industry-wide savings claim; no plant-level measured saving.

evidence_summary: PCA credited a CalPortland executive with coordinating teams promoting PLC acceptance in all 50 states; it reported acceptance by over one-quarter of DOTs since 2012.
interpretation_limit: PCA recognition; does not quantify CalPortland plant production or costs.

source_title: Cement Industry Honors Buzzi Unicem Cement Plant for Innovative Approach to Meeting Its Energy Needs
evidence_summary: Maryneal commissioned a Horomill in 2013; reported grinding power intensity decreased from 78.3 to 47.7 kWh per short ton, approximately 40%.
interpretation_limit: Cement grinding investment; source does not attribute the decision to PLC.

source_title: CalPortland Launches Advancement Environmental Product Line
evidence_summary: CalPortland launched the Advancement PLC product line; it reported approximately 10% lower production CO2 than OPC and positioned PLC as part of carbon reduction strategy.
interpretation_limit: Company-level product launch; no evidence assigning it to Oro Grande or any other plant.

source_title: Greener Cement Achieves Capital Improvement Project
evidence_summary: Monarch used its own raw-materials storage construction project as an opportunity to test lower-carbon cement; source describes raw-material moisture control as an energy and handling consideration.
interpretation_limit: Do not attribute entire storage-facility investment to PLC adoption.

source_title: Mojave Plant Converts to Portland-Limestone Cement
evidence_summary: CalPortland announced conversion of Mojave to PLC; reported approximately 1.3 million tons of annual cement output and a projected 10% reduction in emissions per ton after conversion.
interpretation_limit: Projection, not measured cost savings; webpage lacks visible publication date, so 2022 is inherited from prior dataset.

source_title: Lehigh Cement Plant in Union Bridge Maryland Transitions to EcoCemPLC
evidence_summary: Lehigh announced Union Bridge PLC as primary product by January 2023, projecting avoidance of approximately 126000 tons of CO2 annually.
interpretation_limit: Announced target and projected emissions, not independently measured savings.

source_title: Lehigh Cement Plant in Union Bridge Maryland Transitions to EcoCemPLC
evidence_summary: Lehigh reported production exceeding 2 million tons of PLC in 2021 and expected more than double that in 2022.
quantitative_unit: tons PLC produced in 2021, greater than
interpretation_limit: Company-wide quantity; do not allocate to Union Bridge.

evidence_summary: Argos explicitly linked PLC clinker substitution with replacing an expensive input by lower-price additions, higher sales margins, import substitution and portfolio optimization. It reported Roberta, Harleyville and Newberry conversions in 2022.
economic_mechanism: lower clinker input cost; margins; import substitution
interpretation_limit: Company-wide rationale; not a measured margin at any one plant.

evidence_summary: Martin Marietta described Midlothian finishing capacity expansion expected mid-2024, adding 0.5 million tons annually, and separately reported Type IL production at Midlothian and Hunter.
interpretation_limit: Expansion and Type IL co-occur in report; source does not say expansion was specifically caused by PLC.

evidence_summary: Midlothian new finish mill and silos responded to regional demand. Project was ready in late 2019, paused during COVID, then faced higher costs, longer delivery times and contractor shortages. New mill estimated to save 4 kWh per ton of cement.
economic_mechanism: market demand; capex delays; electricity efficiency
interpretation_limit: General cement finishing investment; not demonstrated PLC-specific.
